risks.title: Repeated net losses and uncertain profitability
risks.summary: The company has accumulated losses for several years and does not guarantee sustainable profitability, threatening its long-term viability.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is at the top of the document and mentions significant losses over multiple years with an accumulated deficit of $2.3B. The language emphasizes uncertainty about future profitability. The 'Capital' category is heavily weighted here due to financial viability. Central placement in the 10-K and strong language ('may not be able to achieve or maintain profitability') justify maximum severity. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Potential failure of the SaaS Counterpart Assistant launch
risks.summary: The development of the SaaS offering for external partners is risky: its failure could jeopardize future growth.
risks.score_rationale: The launch of Counterpart Health is presented as strategic but with high uncertainty regarding adoption, costs, and execution. Repeated mentions across sections with concerning language ('may not be successful', 'could harm our reputation'). Existential risk due to economic model diversification. High placement in the document and product novelty justify high severity. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Difficulty in physician adoption of Clover Assistant
risks.summary: If physicians do not adopt or use Clover Assistant sufficiently, expected medical cost benefits will not be realized.
risks.score_rationale: Several paragraphs detail adoption barriers (EHR integration, perception, training, competition). Repetitive and concerning language ('decline in lives under management', 'frustrating experience'). This risk is central because the entire model's effectiveness depends on prescriber usage. 'Technology' category moderately weighted, but operational impact is high. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Poor control of medical costs (MCR)
risks.summary: Inability to forecast and manage medical costs could impair profitability, especially if AI benefits fail to materialize.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is cited as critical to profitability ('profitability could decline'). Depends on external factors (inflation, regulation) and internal factors (AI adoption, care management). Strong language ('materially and adversely affect'). Directly tied to the health insurance business model. Key placement in the document and direct impact on cash flows justify maximum severity. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Risk of non-compliance with healthcare regulations
risks.summary: Handling sensitive health data exposes the company to growing legal and regulatory risks, especially with the SaaS offering.
risks.score_rationale: Multiple references to risks related to health data privacy (HIPAA, CMS) and regulatory requirements. Concerning language ('significant liability', 'reputational harm'). SaaS expansion increases exposure. While not framed as existential, regulatory impact can be severe. 'Regulation' category moderately weighted, but context is sensitive in healthcare. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Dependence on senior enrollee retention
risks.summary: Profitability depends on senior loyalty: their departure would undermine returns on preventive care investments.
risks.score_rationale: The document emphasizes that long-term value depends on retaining elderly members. If patients leave, preventive care investments are not recouped. Explicit language ('we would not be compensated'). Direct impact on clinical program profitability. 'Industrial' category moderately weighted, but structural risk is strong. (default score, to be refined)
